newsitem.title: UK: London emerging debt eases after NY selling frenzy.
newsitem.headline: London emerging debt eases after NY selling frenzy.

text.p: Emerging debt prices eased into the London trading morning after Tuesday's heavy sell off in New York, but traders said they expected to see some buying at current low levels.
"There's some weakness across the board this morning, but we would expect people to be coming in at these low prices," said one Latin American economist here.

He said Brazil "C" bonds and Mexican paper were likely to benefit from bargain-hunting after Tuesday's hectic profit-taking in New York, though Russian paper could suffer a little from yesterday's Latin weakness.
Latin American Bradys suffered severely as New York traders threw in positions that so far this year had offered high returns.
Brazil sparked the trouble after it posted a poorer than expected weekly October trade figure. But London analysts were surprised by the extent of the fall.
"There is a feeling the U.S. market overreacted on the Brazilian trade figure -- it was a strange focus to take, to look at the weekly figure," the economist said.
"The monthly figures are deteriorating, but you have to look at the full year trade deficit and weigh it up against the level of reserves, which are close to $60 billion," he added.
"You would expect the trade and current account deficit in Brazil to be offset by its capital account surplus."
Brazil C bonds BR8D14=RR were quoted bid side at 69-3/8, down 1/8 from yesterday's New York close. Mexican Pars MX625L19=RR were quoted on screen 1/4 weaker at 68-5/8.
Argentina's launch earlier today of a 30-year 500 million mark Eurobond had little market impact, as Brady traders wait to see how well the issue performs.
The country is also due to launch a Euroyen deal on Thursday.
"If those deals go well, that will signal there is still interest in Argentina and give a lift to Brady prices, but if they go badly that will be a negative sign for the Bradys," said one trader.
Argentine Discs AR425C23=RR lost 1/2 from their New York closing levels, bid in London at 70-1/8.
One trader said softness in Latin paper could impact on Russia debt during the London trading day, but added, "We still think Russia has higher to go."
Russian dollar Vnesh RUVNUSLNS=RR lost about 3/4 from New York's close, bid at 77-1/4 in London. MinFins also weakened with the MinFin 3 RU3E99=RR quoted on screen at 81-1/2 after shedding 1/2 point.
But Latin America players in particular are already starting to look ahead to U.S. data due next week.

Employment data due on Tuesday and Friday, and GDP numbers on Wednesday will impact on Treasuries and have a heavy influence on Bradys, dealers said. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
